correctness.rationale: For paths and nontriangular cycles, every survivor edge between matching endpoints corresponds to exactly one unit gap and two such cross-edges cannot share endpoints. The grown graph has exactly one triangle per cross-edge and no other triangle. Thus winning one-round plans exist iff at least two unit gaps occur, and the ordered-partition formula follows by exact inclusion--exclusion on disjoint triangles. Stars-and-bars for the linear gaps and cyclic compositions with a distinguished matched edge give the full integer coefficient arrays, including the two \(C_4\) alternating perfect matchings. Extracting at least two marked gaps from the formal series yields the two stated rational generating functions. Conditional assignment success probability and the positive-root comparison yield the exponential limit. Actual direct enumeration checked 9945 matching choices across 28 graph cases, 85 exhaustive ordered-partition enumerations on cases containing triangles, and 113 rigorously triangle-free shortcut cases, and 112 formal-series specializations. The proof, not these finite computations, handles all admissible orders.

value.rationale: This is the complete first-round strategy profile for two basic infinite seed families in a newly introduced constrained graph game. The exact number of winning matching choices at every size and the exact count of all subsequent successful binary partitions quantify strategy redundancy that is not captured by the published existence threshold. The exponential success theorem further shows that typical unoptimized first-round play succeeds on long paths and cycles. The common rational denominator and anomalous \(C_4\)/\(C_5\) boundary arise from a specific cross-edge/unit-gap structural correspondence. These motivate the precise invariant independently of its computability, rather than being arbitrary finite counts.
